title: Brother 1.0.20 orchestrator task
description: ORCH-01. One executable unit inside a night run: what it is, what it may touch, how it is checked, and who may work and review it. task_class and evidence_obligation are enum-constrained to exactly the sets scripts/orchestrator_invariants.py holds (TASK_CLASSES, EVIDENCE_OBLIGATIONS); scripts/test_orchestrator_protocol.py asserts this schema's enums equal those sets, so the two can never drift apart silently. scripts/orchestrator_protocol.py enforces this file generically over type, required, properties, enum, const, additionalProperties, items, minItems and minimum.

id.description: Stable identifier for this unit, unique within its run. Names the same join key orchestrator-event-v1.json's action envelope calls task_id; the two schemas spell it differently because the reference is cross-document, not because they mean different things (adversarial review finding 5).

objective.description: What this unit must be true of the world when it is done.

depends_on.description: Ids of units this one may not start ahead of. May be empty for a unit with no prerequisite.

owns.description: The exhaustive list of paths this unit may write. A write to any other path quarantines the result even when the unit's own check passes, so this list can never be empty.

done_check.description: The exact runnable command that decides whether this unit passed. Never empty: a unit with no runnable check has no way to be told apart from one that was never tried.

task_class.description: Must equal scripts/orchestrator_invariants.py's TASK_CLASSES. An unrecognised value is refused, never silently read as implementation.

risk_class.description: How costly a wrong result would be, which decides review depth and retry policy.

evidence_obligation.description: Exactly three levels, matching scripts/evidence_obligation.py's LEVELS, the estate's one frozen definition site for this vocabulary (docs/decisions/evidence-vocabulary-2026-09-13.json, decision EV-3) and the set scripts/orchestrator_invariants.py's EVIDENCE_OBLIGATIONS derives from. There is no REQUIRED_FOR_DELIVERY: an earlier draft of this schema carried a fourth level that scripts/evidence_obligation.py's own validate_obligations refuses as an unknown level, which would have made a task schema-valid and ungateable at once. An unrecognised value is refused, never silently read as OPTIONAL.

worker_profile.description: Which worker tier and effort this unit is dispatched at, for example sonnet-high.

review_profile.description: Which reviewer tier and effort checks this unit, for example opus-high.

max_outer_attempts.description: How many outer attempts this unit gets before it is parked.

max_repair_attempts.description: How many repair attempts a REPAIRABLE verdict on this unit gets. Zero is valid: some units go straight to replan with no repair step.

leaf_worker_only.description: True when this unit must be executed by a leaf worker that cannot itself spawn another coding agent.

orchestrator_preference.description: Optional preferred orchestrator identity for this unit, when one orchestrator is better positioned to hold it.

allow_cross_orchestrator_takeover.description: Optional. Whether a different orchestrator than the preferred or claiming one may take this unit over, for example after the claiming orchestrator's lease expires.
